Ground truth read directly out of the cached zh-cn (Chinese-locale) page HTML: JSON-LD/Livewire structured data states `alternateName`/`productLabel` = "BNN 520-UB-25", `sku`/`mpn`/`orderCode` = "BNN000W", `Brand` = "Balluff". The page also renders a Livewire cookie-consent dialog with `aria-label="Cookie 设置"` and a `Cookie 设置:` heading followed by a `

` whose Chinese consent text repeats the untranslated English loanword "Cookie" five times (`... Cookie 外 ... 其他 Cookie 及类似技术 ... Cookie 政策和隐私政策。 必要 Cookie 分析 功能 Cookie ...`).

_notes.why: Real Balluff zh-cn (Chinese-locale) product page — the generic HTML sweep's `li,p` splitNameValue pass turned the page's Livewire cookie-consent dialog into a `Text` attribute named `Cookies Cookie 设置` with the full Chinese consent paragraph as its value. Existing English-only boilerplate filters (spec-plausibility.ts's `cookie (?:policy|notice|settings)`) never match because the Chinese banner translates "settings" to "设置" and only keeps the technical word "Cookie" itself untranslated — a real gap in the existing (English-keyword) guard, not covered by any prior fixture.
_notes.fix: spec-plausibility.ts's boilerplate label/value check now also rejects text where the literal word "Cookie"/"Cookies" (case-insensitive, ASCII word-boundary — safe because the surrounding script is otherwise non-Latin) appears 2+ times, since this vendor's product domain (industrial connectors/sensors/cam belts) has no legitimate reason to mention the word even once, let alone repeatedly. A single incidental mention still passes.
